text:
finpay-ops: Hey team, production started returning 429s ~09:10 UTC for our /v1/generate calls. No deploys. We're seeing ~3-4% error rate, customer-facing.

finpay-ops: Sample curl: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.finpay\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'` -> response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-ratelimit-rpm: 60
x-rw-ratelimit-tpm: 100
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-retry-after: 8
X-Request-ID: req_01F3ZQ8Q2`

maya (Support): Thanks, sending to SRE + Eng. Can you paste a short timeseries of requests/min from your side (client) and server side (if you have)? Also sample user-agent/version from failing requests.

finpay-ops: Client shows steady 55 rpm avg but periodic microbursts of 10-20 reqs in 2s windows at the top of each minute (cron-ish fanout). User-agent `finpay-sdk/2.4.1`

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-832. Pager duty alerted.

sam (SRE): On Redwood side I'm seeing the API key counted per-key per-minute and per-10minutes windows. Your key hit `rpm=60` ceiling at 09:09:58 and again at 09:10:59. The server enforces both RPM and TPM, and the 0 remaining indicates per-minute limit.

sam (SRE): Root cause hypothesis: client microbursts align to minute boundaries causing your per-minute bucket to exhaust even though average RPM < limit. TPM (10-min) is fine.

raj (Eng): Can you confirm if you're using HTTP/2 multiplexing or multiple concurrent keepalive connections? That affects how we see bursts vs steady.

finpay-ops: We're using finpay-sdk which opens 6 persistent connections and parallelizes small requests. We also have a lambda that fans out to 20 connections for batch work at the minute boundary.

maya (Support): Two parallel mitigations: quick customer-facing fix = ask them to smooth/fuzz schedule to avoid exact minute alignments or set jitter; recommended config change = reduce SDK concurrency / use token-based per-worker rate-limiter. Longer term = we can increase RPM or set a short burst window.

sam (SRE): Repro steps we used: 1) Replay a client trace with same concurrency: `ab -n 100 -c 20 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk.finpay' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` 2) Observe x-rw-ratelimit-remaining drops to 0 for that minute. 3) Check /metrics (redwood.ingress.requests_per_minute{api_key=\"sk.finpay\"}) and `rate()` shows spikes at minute boundary.

sam (SRE): Quick mitigation we can offer from our side: bump their RPM from 60->120 for 24h while they rollout smoothing; or enable a short burst allowance setting (if allowed on their plan) that tolerates short spikes and evens out counts. Need approval from billing for permanent bump.

raj (Eng): Also, if their SDK creates new tokens often (short-lived credentials) each new token may be counted separately if misconfigured — confirm they reuse the same API key and not creating ephemeral keys repeatedly.

finpay-ops: We do rotate worker tokens every 5 minutes for security. Could that be flipping counters?

raj (Eng): The platform counts at the API key surface. If you issue new API keys rapidly, each key has its own small quota; rotating too fast increases management overhead but shouldn't artificially create extra 429s unless your orchestration creates more parallel clients. The rotation every 5m shouldn't cause minute-boundary spikes by itself.

maya (Support): Action items: 1) finpay-ops: add jitter to cron fanouts (+random 0-30s) and reduce parallelism from 20->6 for next 2 hours. 2) finpay-ops: paste one sample failing request headers including User-Agent and X-Request-ID. 3) SRE: consider granting temporary RPM bump for 24h. 4) Eng: validate if we can apply short burst smoothing in the ratecalc to avoid hard minute boundaries.

finpay-ops: Pasted a failing header earlier, sample X-Request-ID `req_01F3ZQ8Q2`. We'll deploy jitter now.

ops-bot: finpay-ops changed channel topic: \"working on jitter rollout\"

sam (SRE): FYI I'll attach logs for that request id: `/var/log/ingress/2026-03-07.log` lines -> `req_01F3ZQ8Q2 09:09:58 GET /v1/generate 429 rpm=60 rem=0`. Also a trace shows 18 concurrent requests from same IP at 09:09:58.

maya (Support): If customer wants immediate relief and they are on Dedicated or higher tier, we can do an emergency RPM increase. For hosted customers, policy requires escalation to billing.

finpay-ops: Jitter deploy done. Observing drop in minute spikes in our metrics. Will monitor next 5 mins.

sam (SRE): Next steps from us: 1) monitor their key `rate()` for next 10m; 2) if 429s persist, we can open a short-lived RPM bump and rollback when they finish rollout. 3) longer term, recommend client-side token bucket smoothing or using Redwood SDK client-side throttler (we have sample code).

raj (Eng): Sample client-side throttler snippet: ```python
# simple token-bucket smoothing
import time
capacity = 60
tokens = capacity
last = time.time()
def allow(n=1):
    global tokens, last
    now = time.time()
    tokens = min(capacity, tokens + (now-last)*(capacity/60))
    last = now
    if tokens >= n:
        tokens -= n
        return True
    return False
```

finpay-ops: Thanks, disabling the high-parallel lambda and enabling jitter fixed the immediate 429s. Error rate back to 0.2%. We'll follow up about a permanent config.

maya (Support): Closing the incident once you confirm 1h stable. Leaving notes: root cause = client-side minute-aligned microbursts exhausting per-minute quota (rpm). Mitigations = client jitter + concurrency cap, temporary RPM bump option, consider platform-level burst smoothing.

finpay-ops: Confirmed stable at 1h. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-832 marked resolved by maya.
